models_evaluated: four deep learning chest radiograph classifiers

links.outcome: Classifier accuracy, sensitivity, specificity on external local hospital dataset
links.effect: Classifiers demonstrated 68%-77% accuracy, 64%-75% sensitivity, and 82%-94% specificity on the external testing dataset.
links.quote: Classifiers demonstrated 68%-77% accuracy, 64%-75% sensitivity, and 82%-94% specificity on the external testing dataset.

links.outcome: Performance differences across patient, setting, and pathology subgroups
links.effect: Decreased sensitivity for solitary findings (43%-65%), patients younger than 40 years (27%-39%), and emergency department patients (38%-60%); decreased specificity on normal radiographs with support devices (59%-85%).
links.quote: Algorithms showed decreased sensitivity for solitary findings (43%-65%), patients younger than 40 years (27%-39%), and patients in the emergency department (38%-60%) and decreased specificity on normal chest radiographs with support devices (59%-85%).

links.outcome: Hidden subgroup performance gaps masked by aggregate metrics
links.effect: Sensitivity dropped for age <40 (27%-39%), ED patients (38%-60%), solitary findings (43%-65%); sex and ancestry differences reflected movements along ROC curve.
links.quote: Differences in sex and ancestry represented movements along an algorithm's receiver operating characteristic curve.

screen.reason: Retrospective external validation and subgroup equity/generalization analysis of four chest radiograph classifiers across patient, setting, and pathology subgroups.
